target_reference_entry:
[23] C. Wang et al., “Thru-the-wall eavesdropping on loudspeakers via RFID
by capturing sub-mm level vibration,” inProc. ACM Interactive Mobile
Wearable Ubiquitous Technol., vol. 5, no. 4, pp. 1–25, 2021.
paper_level_summary_zh: 该文在相关工作部分将目标论文列为RFID声学窃听方法之一，但指出其需要预装RFID标签、实用性较低，且受限于低数据包率和长波长导致的振动分辨率不足。

evidences.evidence_quote: [23] utilizes RFID tags and cGAN to perform acoustic eavesdropping, but this approach is less practical as it requires pre-installing RFID tags near the target.
evidences.evidence_context: Similarly, [22] employs the same wireless-based technology to capture audio with frequencies below 400 Hz. These methods cannot recover human speech due to the low frequency response. [23] utilizes RFID tags and cGAN to perform acoustic eavesdropping, but this approach is less practical as it requires pre-installing RFID tags near the target. Overall, these methods based on WiFi signals and impulse radio [14], [15], [21], [22], [23] are limited by the inadequate vibration resolution caused by low packet rates and long wavelengths.

evidences.why_this_judgment_zh: 正文中[23]明确指向目标论文，描述其方法并指出局限性，属于普通相关工作引用，没有确认亚毫米级能力或正面性能。 普通相关工作不能作为推荐纳入强证据。
